author: William Shakespeare
original_text:
Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Thou art more lovely and more temperate.
Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
And summer's lease hath all too short a date.
good_morning_message: Like a summer's day, this morning holds beauty beyond measure. Step into it with wonder.

author: Robert Frost
original_text:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I —
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.
good_morning_message: Every morning offers a fork in the road. Choose the path that speaks to your heart.

author: William Blake
original_text:
To see a World in a Grain of Sand
And a Heaven in a Wild Flower,
Hold Infinity in the palm of your hand
And Eternity in an hour.
good_morning_message: Look closely at the world this morning — infinity is hidden in the smallest things.

author: William Shakespeare
original_text:
This above all: to thine own self be true,
And it must follow, as the night the day,
Thou canst not then be false to any man.
good_morning_message: Begin this day anchored in who you truly are. Authenticity is your greatest strength.

source: I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud
author: William Wordsworth
original_text:
I wandered lonely as a cloud
That floats on high o'er vales and hills,
When all at once I saw a crowd,
A host, of golden daffodils.
good_morning_message: Step outside this morning and let nature surprise you. Beauty awaits around every corner.

author: Mary Oliver
original_text:
Tell me, what is it you plan to do
with your one wild and precious life?
good_morning_message: This morning is part of your one wild and precious life. What will you do with it?

author: John Keats
original_text:
A thing of beauty is a joy for ever:
Its loveliness increases; it will never
Pass into nothingness.
good_morning_message: Seek beauty this morning — it compounds with time and never truly fades.

author: Walt Whitman
original_text: I am large, I contain multitudes.
good_morning_message: You are vast. Every contradiction within you is part of your wholeness.

source: Hope is the thing with feathers
author: Emily Dickinson
original_text:
Hope is the thing with feathers
That perches in the soul,
And sings the tune without the words
And never stops at all.
good_morning_message: Hope needs no reason. It simply sings — and it is singing in you right now.

author: Rumi
original_text:
Out beyond ideas of wrongdoing and rightdoing,
there is a field.
I'll meet you there.
good_morning_message: Let this morning be that field — beyond judgment, open, and full of light.

author: Kahlil Gibran
original_text:
Your joy is your sorrow unmasked.
And the selfsame well from which your laughter rises
was oftentimes filled with your tears.
good_morning_message: Every sorrow you have carried has deepened your capacity for joy. This morning, let it overflow.

author: Kahlil Gibran
original_text:
And forget not that the earth delights to feel your bare feet
and the winds long to play with your hair.
good_morning_message: The earth is waiting for you this morning. Step out and be welcomed.

author: Walt Whitman
original_text:
I exist as I am, that is enough,
If no other in the world be aware I sit content,
And if each and all be aware I sit content.
good_morning_message: You are enough — exactly as you are, right now, in this morning moment.

author: Marcus Aurelius
original_text:
You have power over your mind — not outside events.
Realize this, and you will find strength.
good_morning_message: The morning is yours to shape. Nothing outside can disturb the calm you choose.

author: Marcus Aurelius
original_text:
Waste no more time arguing what a good man should be.
Be one.
good_morning_message: Less thinking, more becoming. Today, be the person you most admire.

author: Marcus Aurelius
original_text: The soul becomes dyed with the colour of its thoughts.
good_morning_message: Choose your thoughts carefully this morning — they are painting your day.

author: Henry David Thoreau
original_text:
Go confidently in the direction of your dreams.
Live the life you have imagined.
good_morning_message: This morning, take one step in the direction your heart has been pointing.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
original_text:
What lies behind us and what lies before us
are tiny matters compared to what lies within us.
good_morning_message: The treasure you carry inward is greater than anything morning or evening can take away.

author: Ralph Waldo Emerson
original_text:
To be yourself in a world that is constantly trying
to make you something else is the greatest accomplishment.
good_morning_message: Stay true to yourself today — that is the quiet revolution the world most needs.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
original_text:
Where the mind is without fear and the head is held high,
where knowledge is free — into that heaven of freedom,
my Father, let my country awake.
good_morning_message: Walk into this morning with your head held high. Knowledge and courage are your birthright.

author: Rabindranath Tagore
original_text:
Let your life lightly dance on the edges of time
like dew on the tip of a leaf.
good_morning_message: Be light this morning — present, tender, and unhurried as a drop of dew.

author: Swami Vivekananda
original_text: Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.
good_morning_message: The morning is your call to action. Arise — the goal is within reach.

author: Swami Vivekananda
original_text:
Take up one idea. Make that one idea your life;
think of it, dream of it, live on that idea.
Let the brain, muscles, nerves, every part of your body,
be full of that idea, and just leave every other idea alone.
good_morning_message: Choose one thing to give your whole self to today. Singular focus is the seed of mastery.

author: Gerard Manley Hopkins
original_text:
The world is charged with the grandeur of God.
It will flame out, like shining from shook foil.
good_morning_message: Everything around you is charged with glory this morning. Open your eyes to it.

author: Pablo Neruda
original_text:
I want to do with you
what spring does with the cherry trees.
good_morning_message: Be to someone what spring is to blossoms — awakening, gentle, and life-giving.

author: W.B. Yeats
original_text:
The trees are in their autumn beauty,
the woodland paths are dry,
under the October twilight the water
mirrors a still sky.
good_morning_message: Even in stillness, the world is breathtaking. Pause this morning and truly see.

author: Hafiz
original_text:
Even after all this time,
the sun never says to the earth,
'You owe me.'
Look what happens with a love like that —
it lights the whole sky.
good_morning_message: Give today without keeping score. That is the kind of love that lights everything.

source: Tao Te Ching, Chapter 8 (tr. Stephen Mitchell)
author: Lao Tzu
original_text:
The supreme good is like water,
which nourishes all things without trying to.
It is content with the low places that people disdain.
good_morning_message: Be like water this morning — nourishing, effortless, and unbothered by position.

source: Tao Te Ching, Chapter 16 (tr. Ursula K. Le Guin)
author: Lao Tzu
original_text:
Returning to the root is called stillness.
Stillness is called returning to one's destiny.
good_morning_message: Come back to your centre this morning. Stillness is where your truest self waits.

author: John Keats
original_text:
Beauty is truth, truth beauty — that is all
Ye know on earth, and all ye need to know.
good_morning_message: Seek truth today. In it, you will find all the beauty you need.

author: William Blake
original_text:
Tyger Tyger, burning bright,
In the forests of the night;
What immortal hand or eye,
Could frame thy fearful symmetry?
good_morning_message: Step into this new day with the fearless fire of the tiger. You were made for something magnificent.

source: i carry your heart with me
author: e.e. cummings
original_text:
i carry your heart with me (i carry it in
my heart) i am never without it (anywhere
i go you go, my dear; and whatever is done
by only me is your doing, my darling)
good_morning_message: You carry within you everyone who has ever loved you. Begin this morning knowing you are not alone.

author: Maya Angelou
original_text:
You may write me down in history
With your bitter, twisted lies,
You may trod me in the very dirt
But still, like dust, I'll rise.
good_morning_message: Whatever yesterday held, today you rise again. That is your power.

author: Oriah Mountain Dreamer
original_text:
It doesn't interest me what you do for a living.
I want to know what you ache for,
and if you dare to dream of meeting
your heart's longing.
good_morning_message: This morning, ask yourself what you truly ache for. That longing is your compass.

author: Mary Oliver
original_text: I don't want to end up simply having visited this world.
good_morning_message: Don't just pass through today. Inhabit it fully — with your whole heart and senses.
